newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms on IPE, but oversupply pressures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms on IPE, but oversupply pressures.

text.p: NWE gas oil firmed slightly on Thursday as benchmark IPE futures reversed some of Wednesday's losses but premiums stagnated, traders said.
July IPE gas oil settled 75 cents higher at $159.50 a tonne having closed $5.0 lower on Wednesday.
The heating oil barge market was subdued. A German player sold a 5,000-tonne barge parcel at July IPE -50 cents fob ARA. Other deals at this level were also talked.
Premiums were generally talked at around July IPE -75 cents/flat fob ARA for June delivery and July IPE -50 cents/+25 cents fob ARA for first half July.
Low sulphur diesel barges were quoted around July IPE +$4.50/$5.50 fob ARA for June delivery.
The cargo market continued to be under pressure from imported Russian and Mediterranean material, although Med players said they thought less of their material would head north in July.
Low sulphur diesel premiums continued to be quoted at July IPE +$5.0/+$6.0 cif NWE.
Russian material was quoted around the July IPE +$1.50/flat cif NWE. "There's just too much of it coming in," said one trader.
A couple of Canadian cargoes were also reported to be on the water although details about their fate were hazy.
Low sulphur diesel cargo premiums were quoted around the July IPE +$5.0/+$6.0 level. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
